races.title: State Assembly, District 44
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Nicholas "Nick" Schultz
cands.bio: Democrat representing California Assembly District 44 since December 2024. Former Burbank City Council member and mayor. Previously a California Deputy Attorney General in the Special Prosecutions Section, and earlier a deputy district attorney in Oregon. Chairs the Assembly Public Safety Committee.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

His own 2026 survey lists endorsements from U.S. Sen. Adam Schiff, Attorney General Rob Bonta, Secretary of State Shirley Weber, California YIMBY, California Professional Firefighters, SEIU California and Planned Parenthood. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We could not find his city of birth, where he grew up, or when he moved to California; his campaign site says only that a single mother largely raised him and that he attended the University of Oregon. We found no independent records of his City Council actions or of the bills he sponsored as an Assemblymember. We found no documented statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, H-1B visas, guns, abortion or school choice. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or specific stances on development limits. Claims about his Burbank record, such as housing votes, crime and homelessness reductions and budget results, come only from his own survey answers.

local.label: Roots 20: Ballotpedia says he was born in California, but his upbringing and the date he moved back are not documented; the record shows him living in Burbank as an adult only since his 2020 election to the city council, after he attended college and law school and worked as a prosecutor in Oregon.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024; elected to the Burbank City Council in 2020 and served as mayor; Deputy Attorney General (public corruption and financial fraud prosecutions); previously a deputy district attorney in Oregon; J.D., University of Oregon, 2013.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service at the state and city level and a law career as a prosecutor. He also describes managing a city budget as a council member. His committee chair role was not counted.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service at the state and city level and a law career as a prosecutor. He also describes managing a city budget as a council member. His committee chair role was not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: In his own Ballotpedia survey he says that on the Burbank City Council he helped re-allocate $2 million from the police budget to other city services. He also says crime fell during his time on the council. This is self-reported and was not checked against council records.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Ballotpedia says he was born in California, but his upbringing and the date he moved back are not documented; the record shows him living in Burbank as an adult only since his 2020 election to the city council, after he attended college and law school and worked as a prosecutor in Oregon.

cands.name: Carolyn Daniels
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California Assembly District 44 in 2026. Her campaign site describes her as an independent contractor, wife and mother, and a longtime advocate for women and families. It says she founded Safe Places for Abused Women and Children. She has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements and voter-guide recommendations from Reform California and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn. It also lists voter-guide groups: April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Carolyn Daniels was born or raised, or when she first came to California. Her campaign biography says only that she has lived in the district for 20 years and was raised in a farming and ranching family. No record shows she has held elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated position from her on data centers, foreign or investor ownership of land or homes, guns, abortion, school choice or H-1B and immigration enforcement. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her biography, including her advocacy work and the Miss America claim, comes only from her campaign site, and we found no independent reporting to confirm it.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign biography says she has lived in the 44th Assembly District for 20 years, and it gives no birthplace, upbringing location or earlier California residence.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Self-described independent contractor and advocate for women, children and families; her campaign site says she founded Safe Places for Abused Women and Children in 1992 and toured schools and state legislatures promoting an education initiative. No elected office or legislative, policy or budget job is documented.
qual.why: There is no legislative service and no documented policy, law or budget career. Her advocacy and contracting work is largely unrelated to writing law and budgets, and the details come only from her own campaign site.
qual.label: There is no legislative service and no documented policy, law or budget career. Her advocacy and contracting work is largely unrelated to writing law and budgets, and the details come only from her own campaign site.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign plan says she would defend Prop. 13 (the property tax assessment cap) and cut the car tax and income tax. It does not call for eliminating homestead property taxes.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign plan says she would build more homes by cutting expensive regulations and streamlining permitting to increase supply.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign plan says she would support Prop. 36 reforms, back police, end "housing first," and enforce anti-camping laws.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: Her campaign biography says she has lived in the 44th Assembly District for 20 years, and it gives no birthplace, upbringing location or earlier California residence.
